subject.title: Transcript redaction corrupts Anthropic/Bedrock reasoning signatures (AIza/LTAI false positive), causing persistent replay_invalid

question: What exact boundary should OpenClaw use when an Anthropic/Bedrock provider-owned signature field looks like a real credential to the redaction engine?
rationale: Current tests intentionally redact credential-shaped provider signature fields, while this issue shows that rule can corrupt legitimate opaque replay bytes; maintainers need to choose the security boundary before automation changes it.

options.title: Route-scoped replay-token preservation
options.body: Preserve only validated opaque replay tokens in direct assistant Anthropic/Bedrock signature slots, then keep all other credential-shaped text redacted.

options.title: Pattern-only hardening
options.body: Tighten vendor-prefix regex case and boundaries while keeping the existing idempotency gate, accepting residual opaque-token false positives if another pattern matches.

options.title: Recovery-only mitigation
options.body: Leave redaction behavior unchanged and only drop or repair corrupted thinking blocks on replay, reducing failures without preventing future transcript poisoning.

recommendation.title: Route-scoped replay-token preservation
recommendation.body: Preserve only validated opaque replay tokens in direct assistant Anthropic/Bedrock signature slots, then keep all other credential-shaped text redacted.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and release/tag context point to vincentkoc as the best available routing owner for the redaction-boundary decision.
